title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 222
paragraphs: From thence and as far as Heliopolis inland, Egypt is broad, and the land is all flat and without springs of water and formed of mud. The road as one goes inland from the sea to Heliopolis is about the same in length as that which leads from the altar of the twelve gods at Athens to Pisa and the temple of Olympian Zeus. Reckoning up, you would find the difference very small by which these roads fail of being equal in length — not more, indeed, than fifteen furlongs; for the road from Athens to Pisa is fifteen furlongs short of being fifteen hundred, while the road to Heliopolis from the sea reaches that number completely.
